methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective observational feasibility study of sentinel lymph node (SN) mapping in 40 non-parotid salivary gland tumors. Standardized protocol: intratumoral injection of Tc-99m tracer, SPECT-CT imaging, intraoperative gamma probe detection, SLNB when indicated. High SN detection rate (85%, 33/39). However, small sample, no control group, no statistical power calculations reported, descriptive statistics only, no formal hypothesis testing.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Feasibility study investigating sentinel lymph node technique for rare non-parotid salivary gland tumors with goal of improving staging accuracy. Identified micrometastases in 5 patients, suggesting potential clinical utility. However, LoE 4 reflects observational feasibility design without intervention comparison or validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods describe imaging protocol and surgical technique. Results show detection rates and SN distribution patterns. However, no adherence to reporting standard identified (should follow STARD for diagnostic accuracy), limited discussion of false negatives/negatives, no data availability statement, sparse statistical reporting.

novelty_literature.justification: Application of SN mapping technique to rare non-parotid salivary gland tumors, extending established methodology. SN techniques well-established in other cancers; contribution is narrow application to specific subgroup rather than methodological innovation.

writing_presentation.justification: Methods clearly describe imaging and surgical protocols. Results presented as percentages and clinical observations. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings for rare tumor population. However, sparse statistical analysis and limited depth in disease context discussion.

key_strengths: Feasibility study addressing understudied rare tumor population (non-parotid salivary gland carcinomas) with novel application of SN mapping technique
High SN detection rate (85%) demonstrates technical feasibility of SPECT-CT imaging combined with intraoperative gamma probe in complex head-neck anatomy
Identification of micrometastases in 7 patients (18% of SLNB cases) suggests potential for improved staging accuracy in rare cancer subset
key_concerns: Small sample (n=40, one excluded) and feasibility design without control group or formal hypothesis testing; no power calculation
Descriptive statistics only; no statistical comparisons or confidence intervals reported for detection rates
No prospective validation or comparison with conventional staging methods; unclear clinical impact of micrometastasis detection
Limited discussion of false negative rate and clinical implications for management decisions
chief_reviewer.rationale: Early-stage feasibility study for rare tumor application. Small sample and descriptive nature limit evidence level. Suitable for Tier 4 specialty journals (surgical oncology/head-neck) with major revisions addressing statistical reporting and clinical outcome validation.
